title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 9
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt: A graph showing product penetration rates in the retail banking sector presents the following data: Current accounts: 100%, Savings: 74%, Credit cards: 52%, Investments: 31%, Mortgages: 28%. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
options: A. Cannot be determined from the data
E. The value closest to the overall average
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret retail banking data on product penetration rates.

dataContext.data: Current accounts: 100%, Savings: 74%, Credit cards: 52%, Investments: 31%, Mortgages: 28%

questions.prompt: Based on the chart of content viewing patterns data (Drama: 35%, Comedy: 22%, Documentary: 18%, Action: 15%, Other: 10%), which TWO values would combine to equal approximately the average?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret streaming media data on content viewing patterns.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot comparing supplier performance scores across supply chain categories shows: Quality: 87/100, Delivery: 79/100, Price: 83/100, Responsiveness: 91/100, Sustainability: 74/100. If the trend continued, which projection is most consistent?
options: B. The value closest to the overall average
C. Cannot be determined from the data
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret supply chain data on supplier performance scores.

questions.prompt: A graph showing gym membership usage in the fitness sector presents the following data: Peak hours 6-8am: 42%, 12-2pm: 18%, 5-8pm: 56%, 8-10pm: 23%, Other: 12%. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret fitness data on gym membership usage.

questions.prompt: Analysis of incident response times in cybersecurity: Detection: 4.2h, Containment: 2.8h, Eradication: 6.1h, Recovery: 12.4h, Documentation: 3.9h. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret cybersecurity data on incident response times.

questions.prompt: Given property management occupancy rates by building type data: Office A-grade: 94%, Office B-grade: 78%, Retail flagship: 97%, Retail secondary: 81%, Industrial: 89%. In the left column select the highest-performing category; in the right column select the category that improved most year-over-year.

dataContext.data: Office A-grade: 94%, Office B-grade: 78%, Retail flagship: 97%, Retail secondary: 81%, Industrial: 89%

questions.prompt: A retail sales manager reviews quarterly revenue: Q1: $2.4M, Q2: $3.1M, Q3: $2.8M, Q4: $3.6M. Select: (1) the category requiring immediate attention and (2) the category that exceeds the target of the average by the greatest margin.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret retail sales data on quarterly revenue.

questions.prompt: Analysis of patient wait times in hospital operations: Emergency: 45min, Outpatient: 28min, Radiology: 62min, Laboratory: 19min. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret hospital operations data on patient wait times.

questions.prompt: Three data sources on university admissions application success rates are provided: (Memo) Overall performance improved this quarter. (Table) Engineering: 12%, Business: 18%, Arts: 25%, Sciences: 15%, Law: 9%. (Email) Stakeholders express concern about outliers. Which source most directly supports the memo's claim?
options: D. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret university admissions data on application success rates.

questions.prompt: Source 1 (Report): logistics delivery performance shows: On-time: 78%, Early: 8%, Late <1 day: 10%, Late >1 day: 4%. Source 2 (Email): The weakest performer needs a 20% improvement to meet targets. Source 3 (Table): Targets are set at the top-quartile value. Which category needs improvement?
options: E. All three sources are equally relevant

dataContext.data: On-time: 78%, Early: 8%, Late <1 day: 10%, Late >1 day: 4%

questions.prompt: What is the relative ranking of categories in employee performance training completion rates? (1) Sales: 91%. (2) The remaining values follow a consistent trend.

B. Each statement alone is sufficient
C. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
D. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
E. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret employee performance data on training completion rates.
